Walmart (WMT) stock returned 22.5% in the month to November 2, 2026, outpacing a 2.3% loss for the S&P 500. Investors are now paying 46 times Walmart's earnings over the past twelve months, compared with 22.8 times for the median S&P 500 company. This price represents a bet on profit, and management said on its August 20 call that it expects profit to keep growing much faster than sales in the years ahead. How much of that shows up in Walmart's results so far?

Walmart's Operating Profit Outgrew Revenue This Past Year

Over the twelve months to July 31, 2026, Walmart's operating income rose 11.4%, topping 6.2% growth in revenue. The faster profit growth that buyers are paying for has therefore already started to materialize in Walmart's results. Tariff refunds helped lift the latest quarter, and that quarter accounted for a large share of the twelve-month rise in operating income.

Walmart still keeps a thin slice of each sale. The company posted an operating margin of 4.4% over those twelve months, compared with 18.6% for the median S&P 500 company. Walmart stock commands a far higher earnings multiple than the typical S&P 500 company alongside a far lower business margin, making the pace of profit growth particularly important for Walmart.

Where Is Walmart's Extra Profit Coming From?

Membership, advertising and marketplace generated almost half of Walmart's profit growth, management said on the August 20 call, and it expects this to continue. Walmart's global advertising sales, for one, rose 38% in fiscal Q2 2027. Management also said the company is now earning low double-digit incremental margins, meaning the profit on each extra dollar of sales, and that it sees a way to improve them.

The stores themselves are weaker. Management said in-store comparable sales were down by a low single-digit percentage in fiscal Q2 2027, continuing a trend that began late in the previous fiscal year. It said this came mainly from its health and wellness business, where most of those sales happen in stores. Walmart U.S. comparable sales still rose 2.6% in total, led by transactions. Management also said higher fuel prices were putting more pressure on shoppers than at the start of the year. It expects more than $2 billion of extra fuel-related costs this year beyond its original guidance. The best case for the stock therefore lies in the newer businesses, and the clearest risk is weak in-store sales.

What Is Behind The Move In DoorDash Stock?

DoorDash (DASH) stock climbed 6.2% on Monday, November 2, 2026, while the S&P 500 fell 0.5%. On October 29, the company released its quarterly results and agreed to acquire Instacart. It then filed its quarterly report with the SEC on October 30, so those results were already public before Monday's gain. So what did those results show?

DoorDash Grew Sales And Profit In Fiscal Q3 2026

DoorDash posted revenue of $4.62 billion for fiscal Q3 2026, the quarter ended September 30, marking a 34.0% increase from a year earlier. Operating margin, representing the share of sales left after running the business, expanded to 9.6% from 7.5% the prior year. In its October 29 release, the company said the quarter set new records for revenue and net income.

That same day, DoorDash agreed to purchase the online grocery platform Instacart for an equity value of about $17 billion, at least 75% of it in cash. The stock had already risen 5.6% on October 29, a gain news reports linked to the deal, before closing flat on October 30.

On November 2, news reports said DoorDash had begun offering $12 meal deals in some cities: full meals from local restaurants, with no delivery fees.

Other Consumer Stocks Rose, But Less Than DoorDash

DoorDash climbed alongside its group that day, but advanced further. All five companies on its peer list gained, including Walmart, up 3.4%, and Uber, up 2.2%. The SPDR fund for consumer discretionary stocks, XLY, advanced 2.4% during a session when the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.1%. Consumer stocks moved up while the wider market slipped, and DoorDash's gain amounted to more than twice that of the sector fund.

Over Twelve Months, DoorDash Stock Is Down

Investors holding DoorDash stock from October 30, 2025 to November 2, 2026 lost 25.2%, trailing the S&P 500's 11.8% return. Its highest close since November 3, 2025 came that day, at $242.05, and its lowest was $146.60 on March 27, 2026. Shares have partly recovered since hitting that low. From May 4 to November 2 they returned 10.1%, though they lost 6.1% from August 4.

A rise this large is uncommon for DoorDash. It happened in four sessions over the prior 365 days. Including declines, the stock's latest move at least this large was a 7.7% fall on September 28, 2026.

At the November 2 close, DoorDash traded at a valuation of 4.8 times its sales over the past twelve months, compared with 3.3 times for the S&P 500. The company is expected to report its fiscal Q4 2026 results in February 2027, and its operating margin is the measure to watch in that report.

title: Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX Block Their Stock From OKX-ICE Tokenized Venue
detail:
Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX Block Their Stock From OKX-ICE Tokenized Venue

Trading disclosure

Two of Elon Musk's companies are now keeping their shares off OKX and ICE's planned tokenized stock venue.

Tesla and SpaceX are among six new objecting issuers listed in an updated notice from OKXICE TSV dated Monday. Amazon, Netflix, Lam Research, and SoFi Technologies are the others. The additions bring the total to 56 companies.

The list stood at 50 in the venue's Oct. 30 notice, when Nvidia, Costco, and Nike led the biggest batch yet. That followed 38 on Oct. 28, after Walmart joined, and nine on Oct. 15, when the first objectors appeared.

The new names deepen the roster of megacap holdouts. Amazon, Tesla, and Netflix join Microsoft, Alphabet, and Nvidia, while SoFi, a fintech company that offers crypto trading, adds a company with its own stake in digital assets. SpaceX, which trades under the ticker SPCX, rounds out the batch.

Under the SEC's innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party.

If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can't make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC's order. The objection applies only to that venue.

OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX's U.S. holding company, plans to offer tokenized U.S. stocks 24/7 through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on OKX's XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC.

To trade, users must pass identity and sanctions checks and hold a nontransferable "soulbound" token that the venue's smart contracts verify before every transaction.

Nvidia and Nike Lead Biggest Wave Yet of Tokenized Stock Objections

Apple is now one of the few megacap names still missing from the list. And while objections bar OKXICE from listing third-party tokenized versions of a company's stock, they don't close every door.

The notice says the venue can also list shares tokenized by the issuers themselves, though it doesn't identify any, and that tokenized stocks it offers aren't restricted to trading on OKXICE alone.

title: Trump’s FTC Turns to DoorDash’s Pricing and Dasher Pay After the Instacart Deal

Trump’s FTC Turns to DoorDash’s Pricing and Dasher Pay After the Instacart Deal

Trump's FTC Turns to DoorDash's Pricing and Dasher Pay After the Instacart Deal ©svetikd from Getty Images Signature, Volodymyr Melnyk via Canva
Key Takeaways

On Oct. 28, the FTC ordered DoorDash, Instacart, Walmart and six other companies to explain whether they use personal data to set prices and gig-worker pay, a day before DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart for about $17 billion.

The orders are part of a study, and they're unlikely to change DoorDash's fees or Dasher pay anytime soon.

DoorDash's operating margin was about 6% in 2025, and in September it agreed to pay $131.5 million to settle New York City's probe of Dasher pay.

At about 26x forward earnings, near its five-year low, the stock already prices in a lot of risk, and the antitrust review of the Instacart deal is the bigger test ahead.

DoorDash (DASH:NASDAQ) just agreed to pay about $17 billion for Instacart (CART:NASDAQ). Now the Federal Trade Commission wants to see how both companies set prices, and how they pay the people who deliver the orders.

The FTC sent its orders on Oct. 28, the day before DoorDash announced the Instacart deal. Nine companies got them at once, Walmart (WMT:NASDAQ) among them. So the scrutiny of Instacart's pricing now covers DoorDash's own marketplace and its Dasher pay too.

What the FTC wants to know

The orders went to Walmart and Target, Uber and Lyft, Instacart and DoorDash, and three airlines. For the four gig apps, they ask about worker pay as well as prices.

FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson said in the agency's release that it intends "to scrutinize the opaque methodology" some companies may use to set what consumers pay and what gig workers earn. Each company has 45 days from receiving its order to respond.

The orders don't say that anyone uses personalized pricing, and Walmart says it doesn't. "We price the product, not the person," CEO John Furner said in a September letter to customers. Instacart has also denied using personalized pricing.

DoorDash keeps very little of each order

For DoorDash, the pricing and pay under review sit right on top of its profit. In 2025, it kept 13.4% of its $102.0 billion of order value as revenue, and less than a penny of each dollar as net income. Dashers earned over $20 billion that year.

Analysts expect that profit to grow fast. Consensus normalized EPS rises from $5.10 in 2025 to $9.91 in 2028.

Dollar General Corporation DG is strengthening its store modernization strategy through the introduction of DGTP '26, a new store format designed to improve shopping convenience and customer engagement. Introduced in fiscal 2026, the format reflects the company's efforts to make its stores more accessible, easier to navigate and better aligned with customer shopping preferences.

The redesigned layout incorporates customer insights, featuring a more open front-of-store environment and improved sightlines for shoppers and employees. Dollar General has also made significant changes to merchandise adjacencies, creating distinct shopping destinations for food and snacks, health and beauty, and home and seasonal products. These adjustments could encourage customers to explore more categories, supporting additional purchases and stronger sales productivity. DGTP '26 is being introduced through both new store openings and Project Renovate, extending its potential impact across the store network.

Dollar General plans approximately 2,000 Project Renovate remodels in fiscal 2026, targeting an annualized comparable-sales lift of approximately 6% from these projects. While this target is not specific to DGTP '26, the format's integration into the remodel program creates an opportunity to enhance store performance. Sustained customer engagement and broader adoption could establish DGTP '26 as another contributor to long-term sales growth.

How Are Walmart & Target Enhancing Their Store Formats?

Walmart Inc. WMT continues to invest in store remodels and new locations to improve shopping convenience and customer engagement. During the first half of fiscal 2027, Walmart completed approximately 280 store remodels across its U.S. business. Walmart is also investing in omnichannel-enabled stores to support both in-store shopping and digital order fulfillment. These initiatives aim to strengthen store productivity, improve customer convenience and boost sustained sales growth.

Target Corporation TGT is enhancing its in-store shopping experience through merchandise resets and redesigned category destinations. In second-quarter fiscal 2026, Target transformed nearly half of its center-store grocery assortment, improving product presentation and expanding space for snacks, fresh produce and emerging brands. Following these changes, snack sales were running 15% above the prior-year level. Target is also introducing Beauty Studio destinations to strengthen customer engagement and encourage category-specific shopping.

Costco Wholesale (COST) is allocating more money each year to capital projects, the investments it makes in buildings and equipment. During its September 24, 2026 call, management said this spending belongs to a three-year stretch of outsized growth that began in fiscal 2025. This pace matters for a retailer that retains a thin slice of each sale as profit. So how much more is Costco planning to spend in fiscal 2027?

Costco Plans To Spend 17% More In Fiscal 2027

Costco plans about $7.5 billion in capital spending for fiscal 2027, compared with $6.4 billion in fiscal 2026.

Executives detailed the company's building plan for the year on the same call. Management intends to open 33 warehouses in fiscal 2027, including five relocations, as it advances a goal to add 30 net new warehouses a year. At the time of the call, management said Costco operated 939 warehouses worldwide.

How Much Of Costco's Cash Goes Into Building?

Capital spending consumed about 41% of the $15.8 billion in cash Costco generated from operations in fiscal 2026. That share remains worth watching at a retailer with Costco's margins. Over fiscal 2026, Costco recorded a 3.0% net margin, compared with 13.4% for the S&P 500.

The company's cash generation has kept up, however. Cash from operations rose from $13.3 billion a year earlier, so Costco produced more cash even as it spent more on building.

What Does Costco's Share Price Assume About This Spending?

Costco stock trades at 50.1 times its earnings over the last twelve months, compared with 22.8 for the S&P 500. At that price, buyers likely assume the new warehouses will continue adding sales and profit for years.

The company's own cash provides the best evidence that Costco can afford this spending. Free cash flow, the cash remaining after capital spending, rose to $9.38 billion in fiscal 2026 from $7.84 billion a year earlier. Furthermore, Costco held $21.3 billion in cash and short-term investments at the end of fiscal 2026, against $8.58 billion of debt. Management also said it expects growth in capital spending to slow after fiscal 2027.

This makes the worry a mild one for now: Costco is spending more, but its operations also bring in more cash than the company spends. That dynamic would change if spending keeps climbing faster than the cash Costco produces. Costco is expected to report its fiscal Q1 2027 results in December 2026. At that point, capital spending for the quarter, measured against the roughly $7.5 billion planned for the year, is the figure to watch.

title: Walmart driver exposed a $1.4M fraud ring after noticing up to 50 packages piled up at one Arizona home
detail:
Walmart driver exposed a $1.4M fraud ring after noticing up to 50 packages piled up at one Arizona home
Mike Crisolago
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 6:30 AM EST 6 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Jay L Clendenin/Getty Images

It might be the most important delivery of one Walmart [NASDAQ: WMT] driver's career, as it led him to tipping off police in Arizona about a suspicious home with packages piling up on the porch.

The Peoria Police Department said the driver's tip about "delivering numerous packages under different names to a Peoria residence" — which court documents say totalled between 30 and 50 packages — kicked off a two-month investigation that resulted in the arrest of six suspects in a $1.4 million alleged fraud operation.

William Kennedy, a Peoria police officer, told Arizona's Family that, "Without that delivery driver, I don't know if it would have come across our radar." Peoria Police described the unnamed driver as "the wonderful reporting citizen."

The police added that their investigation "identified a network allegedly using stolen credit card information from Walmart customer accounts to purchase merchandise online."

Arizona's Family reports that court documents cite 15,500 orders on Walmart's website allegedly delivered to six different houses. Kennedy said purchases included, "stuff for the dogs, the kids, their house, all those types of items." The outlet also said police confirmed $57,501 in chargeback losses to two Walmart customers, as well as $8,821 in fraudulent purchases impacting 203 JPMorgan Chase customers.

Peoria police added the allegedly stolen items were shipped to Vietnam, and that search warrants recovered around $45,000 worth of gold bars, $35,000 in cash and $25,000 worth of merchandise.

Account takeover fraud is hitting millions

Court documents named the six people charged in the alleged Walmart fraud as Hie Xuan Le, Hailey Hang Nguyen, Hoai Nguyen, Minh Ngoc Nguyen, Uy Vu Phan and Thien Tran, with Arizona's Family adding the charges include identity theft, fraud and trafficking stolen property, among others.

When reached for comment about the alleged thefts and how the company plans to prevent similar fraud in the future, a Walmart spokesperson simply told Moneywise, "We care about our customers and we are committed to helping prevent fraud, and working with law enforcement to hold bad actors accountable."
